title: Motion: describing how things move
objectives: After this lesson you can explain what motion, distance and displacement mean.
After this lesson you can calculate speed, velocity and acceleration using simple formulas.
After this lesson you can read a distance-time graph and say how fast something moves.

sections.title: What motion means
paragraphs: You are in motion when your position changes with time. A bus moving down a road is in motion, and so is a fan blade going around. To say that something moved, we compare its position now with its position a moment ago.
To describe motion clearly we use a few measured quantities. Each one answers a different question: how far, how fast, and speeding up or slowing down. You will meet them one at a time.

sections.title: Distance and displacement
paragraphs: Distance is the total length of the path you travelled. Walk 3 metres forward and then 4 metres back, and your distance is 7 metres. Distance only has a size, so it is called a scalar.

Displacement is the shortest straight line from your starting point to your ending point, with its direction. In the same walk you end up 1 metre behind where you began, so your displacement is 1 metre backwards. Because it carries a direction, displacement is a vector.
Distance and displacement are equal only when the whole path is one straight line with no turning back. The moment you turn, they separate.

sections.title: Speed, velocity and acceleration
paragraphs: Speed tells you how much distance is covered in each second. It is distance divided by time. Cover 100 metres in 20 seconds and your average speed is 5 m/s.
Velocity is speed with a direction attached. A car moving north at 20 m/s and a car moving south at 20 m/s have the same speed but different velocities.

Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes. If a body at rest reaches a speed of 10 m/s in 5 seconds, its velocity changed by 10 m/s in 5 s, so its acceleration is 2 m/s2. A common formula is v = u + a*t, where u is the starting velocity.

sections.title: Reading motion from graphs
paragraphs: A distance-time graph plots distance on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis. The slope of the line tells you the speed: a steep slope means fast motion and a flat line means the object is at rest.
For steady motion the graph is a straight line. When the line curves, the speed is changing, which means the motion is accelerated.

glossary.definition: the shortest straight-line distance from start to end, with its direction
speed in a particular direction; the rate of change of displacement
the rate of change of velocity with time
a quantity that has only a size, such as distance or speed
a quantity that has both size and direction, such as displacement or velocity
